definitions.gloss: end of work; end of the business day; closing
definitions.explanation: The conclusion of work or business hours for the day. Used in both workplace and school contexts. The opposite of 始業 (start of work).

examples.japanese: {終業|しゅうぎょう}{時間|じかん}は{午後|ごご}{五時|ごじ}です。
examples.english: The end of the workday is at 5 PM.

examples.japanese: {終業|しゅうぎょう}のベルが{鳴|な}ったら{帰|かえ}りの{支度|したく}をする。
examples.english: When the closing bell rings, I start getting ready to go home.

examples.japanese: {終業|しゅうぎょう}{後|ご}に{同僚|どうりょう}と{食事|しょくじ}に{行|い}くことになった。
examples.english: I ended up going to dinner with a colleague after work.

notes:
USAGE:
Can function as a する verb ({終業|しゅうぎょう}する). In schools, {終業|しゅうぎょう}{式|しき} (closing ceremony) marks the end of a school term.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {終業|しゅうぎょう}{時間|じかん} (closing time; end of work hours)
- {終業|しゅうぎょう}{後|ご} (after work)
- {終業|しゅうぎょう}{式|しき} (closing ceremony — at school)
- {終業|しゅうぎょう}のチャイム (the end-of-work chime)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {始業|しぎょう}: start of work — the opposite; the beginning of work or class hours
- {退勤|たいきん}: leaving work — the act of physically departing the workplace
